# Module Reference

Every documented source file, grouped by folder. Add a `/** ... @module Name */` block at the top of a file to have it appear here.

## `src/`

### App

`src/App.jsx`

Application shell: a tiny screen router (map ↔ level) plus global overlays —
top bar, instant-feedback pill, toasts, the teacher panel and ink layer.
The current screen is mirrored into the URL hash so refresh/back work:
  #/level/<id>  original games · #/lab/<id> published engine lessons ·
  #/studio      local authoring studio (needs the studio server) ·
  #/review/<id> review preview (only in `npm run build:review` builds).

### main

`src/main.jsx`

Entry point: mounts <App> inside the game state provider and loads styles.

## `src/components`

### Button

`src/components/Button.jsx`

Large, rounded button with variants: primary · secondary · ghost · success.
Plays a soft click sound on press.

### Card

`src/components/Card.jsx`

Glassmorphism card — the basic surface of the UI.

### Checklist

`src/components/Checklist.jsx`

Mini-objective list. Items tick with a pop when `done` becomes true —
small wins inside a step keep momentum up.

### Choices

`src/components/Choices.jsx`

Multiple-choice predictor.

Wrong picks shake, reveal their optional `why`, and lock so the player can try again;
the right pick glows and calls `onSolved`. Scoring goes through the step API,
so combos and stars "just work".

  <Choices api={api} correct="b" onSolved={() => setDone(true)}
           options={[{ id: 'a', label: '4', why: 'That would be adding 2…' }, …]} />

### DrawingOverlay

`src/components/DrawingOverlay.jsx`

Teacher Mode ink layer: a transparent full-screen canvas the instructor can
draw on (over graphs, animations, anything). Only captures the pointer while
drawing is enabled; strokes survive toggling and are wiped by `clearSignal`.

### FeedbackPill

`src/components/FeedbackPill.jsx`

Instant feedback after every answer: "+14 XP · 3× combo" or "Not quite — try again".
Driven by `state.lastGain`, so any step that calls `api.answer()` gets it for free.

### Frac

`src/components/Frac.jsx`

Stacked fraction for use inside <M>: <Frac top="Δy" bottom="Δx" />.

### HintButton

`src/components/HintButton.jsx`

Reveal-on-demand hint. The first reveal registers a hint (costs a star);
the text then stays visible.

### Icon

`src/components/Icon.jsx`

Minimal stroke icon set (24×24, currentColor). Hand-drawn paths keep the
bundle dependency-free and give the UI a consistent, calm line style.

### Insight

`src/components/Insight.jsx`

The "I noticed…" card that appears *after* an interaction.
Keep `children` to 2–3 sentences; `formula` is revealed underneath with a flourish.
`bridge` (real-life context) is shown just before the formula so the equation reads as a conclusion.

### LevelComplete

`src/components/LevelComplete.jsx`

End-of-level celebration: animated stars, XP earned, the big idea recap and
the next action (next level · replay · map).

### MathText

`src/components/MathText.jsx`

Inline math typography: `<M>y = a<sup>x</sup></M>`.
Uses a serif italic face so formulas feel distinct from UI text.
`block` renders it centred on its own line with a gentle reveal animation.

### Plot

`src/components/Plot.jsx`

Function plotter built on <Stage>.

Declarative props describe what to draw in *world* coordinates:
  fns    — [{ f, color, width, dash, domain, glow }]
  points — [{ x, y, color, r, label, ring }]
  lines  — [{ x1, y1, x2, y2, color, width, dash }]
plus an optional `draw(ctx, view)` escape hatch for custom art.
Colours may be CSS colours or theme keys ('accent', 's1'…'s5', 'good', 'bad', 'muted'…).
`onPointer(type, {x, y, px, py}, dragging)` reports pointer events in world units.

### ProgressBar

`src/components/ProgressBar.jsx`

Animated horizontal progress bar (value 0–1).

### Readout

`src/components/Readout.jsx`

Row of labelled live numbers ("time 3.2 s · speed 12 m/s").

### Sketch

`src/components/Sketch.jsx`

Tiny inline curve sketch with a caption, used as a visual answer option
("which shape will appear?") so players compare shapes, not words.

### Slider

`src/components/Slider.jsx`

Labelled range slider with a live value bubble.
Set `hideValue` when the number itself would give away an answer.

### Stage

`src/components/Stage.jsx`

Responsive, high-DPI canvas.

The parent supplies a `draw(ctx, info)` function; it runs after every render and
whenever the canvas resizes, so animating is as simple as updating React state.
Pointer handlers receive coordinates in CSS pixels relative to the canvas.

### Stars

`src/components/Stars.jsx`

0–3 star display; `animate` pops them in one by one.

### StepDots

`src/components/StepDots.jsx`

Row of dots showing progress through a level's steps.
Completed dots fill, the current one pulses. Teacher mode makes them clickable.

### StepLayout

`src/components/StepLayout.jsx`

Standard frame for a step: prompt → interactive stage → insight → continue.

Steps only decide *when* they are `done`; the layout handles hints,
teacher "reveal" mode and the Continue button so every step feels consistent.
Inside a level it also shows the lesson companion: the discovery question
(before any explanation), the Egyptian-Arabic card and the real-life bridge.

### TeacherPanel

`src/components/TeacherPanel.jsx`

Floating control panel for instructors.

 - Pause / resume every animation in the app
 - Draw on top of anything (ink overlay) and clear it
 - Reveal explanations instantly (and skip steps)
 - Skip the current level, jump to any step (via the step dots)
 - Reset all progress

Teacher mode also unlocks every level on the map.

### ToastStack

`src/components/ToastStack.jsx`

Stack of transient notifications (achievements, milestones).

### TopBar

`src/components/TopBar.jsx`

Global header: brand, XP & rank, combo streak, stars and the settings toggles
(sound, theme, teacher mode).

## `src/core`

### GameContext

`src/core/GameContext.jsx`

React glue around the game reducer.

Responsibilities:
 - hydrate state from localStorage and persist changes
 - apply the resolved theme to <html data-theme>
 - keep the sound engine in sync with the sound setting
 - evaluate achievements after every change and surface toasts
 - expose friendly action helpers (`answer`, `hint`, `completeLevel`, …)

### achievements

`src/core/achievements.js`

Achievement catalogue.

Each achievement has a pure `check(state)` predicate. After every state change the
GameContext evaluates the locked ones and unlocks whatever became true — so adding a
new achievement is just adding an object here.

### confetti

`src/core/confetti.js`

Lightweight canvas confetti. Creates a temporary full-screen canvas,
animates a burst of particles and removes itself when finished.
Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` by drastically reducing the burst.

### gameReducer

`src/core/gameReducer.js`

The game's single source of truth.

A plain reducer (no React) so every rule — combos, stars, unlocking, resets —
is unit-testable. Persistent progress and transient session data live side by side;
`persistable()` strips what must not be saved (teacher tools, the current run).

### mathUtils

`src/core/mathUtils.js`

Small numeric helpers shared by the levels.

### scoring

`src/core/scoring.js`

Scoring rules: XP, combo bonus, stars and player ranks.

Kept pure so balancing the game is a matter of editing numbers here
(and the unit tests tell you if you broke something).

### sound

`src/core/sound.js`

Tiny Web Audio synthesiser — every sound effect is generated in code,
so the game ships with zero audio files and works offline.

Call `sound.setEnabled(false)` to mute; `sound.play(name)` is always safe to call.

### storage

`src/core/storage.js`

Safe wrapper around localStorage.

Private windows, blocked cookies or quota errors must never crash the game,
so every access is guarded and falls back to in-memory defaults.

## `src/engine`

### engine/catalog/published

`src/engine/catalog/published.js`

Student-facing catalogue. Bundles content/published/*.json at build time,
then re-checks every lesson on load: schema-valid, status "published", a
recorded human approval, and content matching the approval hash. Anything
else is dropped (and reported in `rejected`) — a file copied into the folder
by hand cannot reach students.

### engine/catalog/reviewPreview

`src/engine/catalog/reviewPreview.js`

Review-preview catalogue — ONLY in builds made with VITE_REVIEW_PREVIEW=1
(`npm run build:review`). It bundles working copies from content/lessons/
that are valid and awaiting review (in_review / approved) so reviewers can
try them from a shareable static link. They render in preview mode (banner,
no progress) and never pass through the student publishing gate.

In normal builds the condition is a compile-time `false`, so no unpublished
lesson is bundled (a test checks the production bundle).

### engine/generation/pipeline

`src/engine/generation/pipeline.js`

Generation pipeline: request → provider (with retries) → parse → sanitise →
validate → save as DRAFT. Never approves or publishes.

Drafts are never lost:
 - the request is recorded before the provider is called;
 - a provider failure only marks that request failed — existing drafts are untouched;
 - output that parses but fails validation is still saved as a draft (with its
   report) so an author can fix it; output that does not parse is kept as raw
   text on the request record.

### engine/generation/prompt

`src/engine/generation/prompt.js`

Builds the provider prompt. The model must return ONE JSON lesson that fits
schema v1 and only uses supported interaction types and named computations.
The author's request is passed as quoted data, never as instructions.

### engine/generation/request

`src/engine/generation/request.js`

Validates an author's generation request. Treated as untrusted input:
bounded lengths, no markup, known student levels, Egyptian Arabic default.

### engine/hash

`src/engine/hash.js`

Deterministic content hashing used to bind an approval to exact content.
Canonical JSON (sorted keys) + cyrb53. This detects any change to approved
content; it is an integrity check, not a security signature.

### engine/interactions/catalog

`src/engine/interactions/catalog.js`

Catalogue of supported interaction types: what each one teaches (skills),
its parameters, and how to validate them. Pure data + validators — no React —
so the schema validator, the generation prompt and the renderer registry all
share one source of truth.

Adding a lesson that only uses these types needs no renderer change. A new
type needs an entry here AND a component in `src/lab/registry.jsx`.

### engine/math/accumulation

`src/engine/math/accumulation.js`

Accumulation maths for flow-rate lessons: a piecewise-linear flow rate Q(t),
its exact integral, rectangle (Riemann) sums and a tank model with explicit
overflow. Pure functions, unit-tested.

Units (by convention across the engine): t in minutes, Q in litres/minute,
volumes in litres.

### engine/math/compute

`src/engine/math/compute.js`

Whitelisted computations that lesson content may reference *by name* to get
a correct answer. Content never contains code or trusted answer numbers:
an assessment says `{ compute: 'riemann', args: {...} }` and the engine
calculates the answer here. Each entry validates its own arguments.

### engine/narration/playback

`src/engine/narration/playback.js`

Playback controller for the explainer: one clock for animation, captions and
narration audio, with play / pause / replay / seek / speed / mute.

Guarantees:
 - Only one playback is active app-wide: starting one pauses any other, so
   narration never overlaps.
 - `dispose()` stops audio and the clock; components call it on unmount
   (i.e. on navigation).
 - With an audio track the clock follows `audio.currentTime` (the recording
   is the master); otherwise a monotonic internal clock is used.

The audio object only needs the HTMLMediaElement subset used here, so tests
can pass a fake.

### engine/narration/timeline

`src/engine/narration/timeline.js`

One timeline drives the explainer: animation scene, captions and narration
all read the same clock value `t` (seconds). These pure helpers turn `t`
into what should be on screen.

### engine/progress/labProgress

`src/engine/progress/labProgress.js`

Progress for engine lessons, stored inside the existing game save under
`lessons` (same storage key and STATE_VERSION as the original game, so old
saves load unchanged and simply gain an empty `lessons` map).

A lesson is complete only when every learning objective has been
demonstrated by at least one *credited* assessment — not when the last scene
is reached. An answer is credited only when it shows the student's own
reasoning: a choice right on the first pick, or a numeric answer right before
its worked explanation was shown (see the assessment components).

  lessons[lessonId] = {
    stage, furthest,                       // stage indices
    attempts: { [assessmentId]: { tries, correct, credited, last, seed } },
    objectives: { [objectiveId]: true },
    completed, completedAt, contentHash
  }

### engine/review/workflow

`src/engine/review/workflow.js`

Review workflow — the single place that decides what a lesson's review
status may become. The server store calls these functions for every write,
and the student-facing loader calls `isPublishable` on every read, so a
lesson can only reach students through draft → in_review → approved →
published with a human reviewer and an approval bound to the exact content.

All functions are pure: they return a new lesson or throw a ReviewError.

### engine/schema/lessonSchema

`src/engine/schema/lessonSchema.js`

Lesson schema v1 and its validator.

Every lesson — AI-generated, imported or hand-authored — is untrusted data
until `validateLesson` passes. The validator is strict: unknown keys,
unsupported interaction types, uncomputable answers, malformed timelines or
unreachable objectives are errors. Soft issues (e.g. unsupported concepts the
author listed) are warnings that a reviewer must acknowledge before approval.

Teaching flow enforced by stage order:
  problem → prediction → experiment → explanation → equation → practice → challenge

## `src/hooks`

### useAnimationFrame

`src/hooks/useAnimationFrame.js`

requestAnimationFrame loop that respects Teacher-mode pause.

`callback(dt, elapsed)` receives seconds since the last frame (clamped so a
backgrounded tab doesn't cause a giant jump) and total running seconds.
While paused or inactive, time does not advance.

### useElementSize

`src/hooks/useElementSize.js`

Tracks an element's content-box size with ResizeObserver.

### useThemeColors

`src/hooks/useThemeColors.js`

Reads the design-token colours from CSS custom properties so canvas drawings
match the current light/dark theme. Recomputes whenever the theme changes.

## `src/lab`

### lab/LessonPlayer

`src/lab/LessonPlayer.jsx`

Generic lesson renderer for validated engine lessons ("Living Lab").

Renders stages in the schema's teaching order, looks up each interaction in
the registry, shows the stage's assessments, and tracks progress through the
shared lab reducer: in the game save for students, in local state for
previews (previews never write progress).

A stage can be left once each of its assessments is resolved (a prediction
only needs an attempt). The lesson completes only when every objective has a
credited answer.

### lab/Notebook

`src/lab/Notebook.jsx`

The notebook margin: objectives with mastery marks, and — collapsed until
wanted — everyday/engineering examples, units, assumptions, model limits and
sources. Explanations stay out of the way of the experiment.

### lab/apparatus/FlowTankView

`src/lab/apparatus/FlowTankView.jsx`

The experiment bench: a tank with a litre scale, inlet valve, flow meter and
overflow pipe, beside the flow-rate graph. Both are drawn from the same
state (time, valve, shading, rectangles), so they can never disagree.

Used by the flow-tank experiment, the animated explainer and the rectangle
stage. Purely presentational: callers own the clock and controls.

### lab/apparatus/useLabColors

`src/lab/apparatus/useLabColors.js`

Reads the Living Lab palette (CSS custom properties on `.lab`) for canvas
drawing, and re-reads it when the theme changes.

### lab/assessments/ChoiceAssessment

`src/lab/assessments/ChoiceAssessment.jsx`

Multiple-choice reasoning question. Each wrong option explains itself and,
when linked, names the misconception behind it. Only a correct FIRST pick
earns mastery credit (no credit for elimination); "حاول تاني" offers a fresh try.

### lab/assessments/NumericAssessment

`src/lab/assessments/NumericAssessment.jsx`

Numeric question with units. The answer is computed by the engine (named
computation), checked within tolerance, and followed by an explanation.
"New values" challenges draw fresh numbers from a seed. A right answer earns
mastery credit only if the worked explanation was not shown yet for these values.

### lab/format

`src/lab/format.js`

Number formatting for the lab (Western digits — as on lab scales and in
Egyptian engineering classes — with thousands separators).

### lab/interactions/EquationInteraction

`src/lab/interactions/EquationInteraction.jsx`

Equation built from safe tokens (always rendered left-to-right inside the
RTL page), with a legend of meanings and units.

### lab/interactions/ExplainerInteraction

`src/lab/interactions/ExplainerInteraction.jsx`

Animated explainer: one `Playback` clock drives the scene (via sceneAt),
the Arabic captions (captionAt) and — when a recording is attached — the
narration audio. Controls: play/pause, replay, mute, speed, seek.
Disposing on unmount stops audio when the student navigates away.

After the explainer, the same simulation opens for free exploration.

An optional browser speech preview exists for authors; it is labelled as a
preview and is not treated as real Egyptian-Arabic narration.

### lab/interactions/FlowTankInteraction

`src/lab/interactions/FlowTankInteraction.jsx`

Experiment: tank and flow-rate graph in sync. Controls (per lesson params):
play/pause the clock, scrub time, open/close the valve (scales Q).

### lab/interactions/RiemannInteraction

`src/lab/interactions/RiemannInteraction.jsx`

Rectangle sums vs the exact integral, with a slider for the number of
intervals and a choice of sample point. A small table shows convergence.

### lab/registry

`src/lab/registry.jsx`

Renderer registry: interaction type → component. Must cover every type in
engine/interactions/catalog.js (a test enforces this). Lessons that use only
these types render with no code changes.

### HyperbolicWorld/StepCircle

`src/levels/HyperbolicWorld/StepCircle.jsx`

Step 3 — Circle vs hyperbola. One slider t drives two points:
(cos t, sin t) on the unit circle and (cosh t, sinh t) on x² − y² = 1.
Shaded sectors have equal area t/2 in both worlds; live readouts let the
player discover which combination stays constant.

`src/levels/HyperbolicWorld/catenary.js`

`src/levels/HyperbolicWorld/index.jsx`

### LightBeam/BeamScene

`src/levels/LightBeam/BeamScene.jsx`

The round room: a flashlight at the centre, its beam and light spot on the
wall, plus optional projections of the spot onto a height ruler (sine) and a
floor ruler (cosine). Reports pointer angles in degrees for aiming/dragging.

### LightBeam/StepAim

`src/levels/LightBeam/StepAim.jsx`

Step 1 — Aim. The light is off. The player taps the wall where they think the
spot will land after a given turn, then switches the light on to check.

### LightBeam/StepCos

`src/levels/LightBeam/StepCos.jsx`

Step 4 — The floor shadow. A second projection onto the floor draws another
wave. The player identifies it as the sine wave shifted a quarter turn: cosine.

### LightBeam/StepHeight

`src/levels/LightBeam/StepHeight.jsx`

Step 2 — Height of the spot. Drag the flashlight around; a ruler shows how
high the spot is. Three goals reveal the key values of sine.

### LightBeam/StepTune

`src/levels/LightBeam/StepTune.jsx`

Step 5 — Tune the wave. Beam length sets the amplitude and spin speed sets
how many waves fit in one turn. Match two ghost waves to earn y = A·sin(kθ).

### LightBeam/StepWave

`src/levels/LightBeam/StepWave.jsx`

Step 3 — Draw the wave. Predict the shape the spot's height will trace, then
spin the light twice and watch the sine wave appear — and repeat.

### LightBeam/WaveTrace

`src/levels/LightBeam/WaveTrace.jsx`

Plot of spot height (and optionally floor position) against total angle
turned, drawn up to the current angle — the wave appears as the light spins.

Level 4 — Light Beam: sine and cosine from circular motion; periodicity.

### SpeedDetective/Road

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/Road.jsx`

Canvas road with a car, optional motion trail and distance markers.
Used as a full road (live playback) or a slim "photo strip" lane.

### SpeedDetective/StepReadSlopes

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/StepReadSlopes.jsx`

Step 4 — Read the slopes. A new trip where the car stops and reverses.
Two quick questions build the rule: flat tangent = stopped, downhill = backwards.

### SpeedDetective/StepTangent

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/StepTangent.jsx`

Step 2 — Steepest point. The trip becomes a position-time graph. Dragging a
marker along it shows a tangent line and the live speedometer: the player
discovers that steepness *is* speed, then locks in the fastest moment.

### SpeedDetective/StepWatch

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/StepWatch.jsx`

Step 1 — Photo finish. Watch the car drive, then study four "long-exposure
photos" and guess which moment was fastest. The trail length is the clue.

### SpeedDetective/StepZoom

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/StepZoom.jsx`

Step 3 — Zoom in. A secant line between two moments gives an *average* speed.
Shrinking the gap makes the secant hug the tangent, and the average settles on
a single number. Only then is the derivative's limit notation revealed.

`src/levels/SpeedDetective/index.jsx`

Level 1 — The Speed Detective: speed as slope, tangents, and the derivative.

### TheSwing/Pendulum

### TheSwing/StepForecast

`src/levels/TheSwing/StepForecast.jsx`

Step 4 — Forecast. Only the first 4 seconds of the graph are known.
Predict the position at 7.5 s using periodicity, then fast-forward to check.

### TheSwing/StepLength

`src/levels/TheSwing/StepLength.jsx`

Step 3 — Longer rope. Two sliders (rope length, pull-back angle) and a live
period readout. Two predictions uncover T = 2π√(L/g) and that amplitude
doesn't matter (for small swings).

### TheSwing/StepPredict

`src/levels/TheSwing/StepPredict.jsx`

Step 1 — Where will it be? Watch one swing (2 s), then for three moments in
time drag a ghost bob to your prediction and release the real pendulum.

### TheSwing/StepTrace

`src/levels/TheSwing/StepTrace.jsx`

Step 2 — Pen on paper. A pen on the bob draws the angle over time.
The player recognises the wave from the Light Beam — and that it's cosine.

### metaRegistry

`src/levels/metaRegistry.js`

Ordered list of level metadata (plain data, no components).

Split from the component registry so core logic (achievements, unlocking)
can know about levels without importing any React code.

### registry

`src/levels/registry.js`

Ordered registry of playable levels: `{ meta, steps }` objects.
Add a level by creating its folder and appending it here and in metaRegistry.js.

### types

`src/levels/types.js`

Shared JSDoc type definitions for levels. No runtime code.

A level is a folder in `src/levels/` with:
  - `meta.js`   — a {@link LevelMeta} object (also read by the docs generator)
  - `index.jsx` — exports `{ meta, steps }` where `steps[i]` renders `meta.steps[i]`

Every step component receives a {@link StepAPI} as its `api` prop.

## `src/screens`

### Home

`src/screens/Home.jsx`

The map: hero with a single obvious "continue" action, the level path,
the achievement shelf and — once everything is solved — the certificate.

### LabScreen

`src/screens/LabScreen.jsx`

Student route for a published engine lesson (#/lab/<id>).

### LabShelf

`src/screens/LabShelf.jsx`

"Living Lab" shelf on the map: lists only lessons that passed the publishing
gate (see engine/catalog/published.js). Shows nothing when none are published.

### LevelScreen

`src/screens/LevelScreen.jsx`

Runs one level: shows the header (title, step dots, progress), renders the
current step with its StepAPI, and shows the completion modal at the end.

Also registers `skipStep` / `skipLevel` handlers for the Teacher panel.

## `src/studio`

### studio/Studio

`src/studio/Studio.jsx`

Authoring studio (#/studio): generate or import → validate → preview →
human review → approve → publish. Talks to the local studio server; every
rule (approval, invalidation, publishing) is enforced there, not by which
buttons are visible here.
